prompt: You climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. In how many distinct ways can you reach step n?
why: ways(n) = ways(n−1) + ways(n−2). Two variables are enough.
trap: Backtracking lists the ways; you only need to count them.

prompt: Rob houses along a street for the most money, but you can't rob two adjacent houses.
trap: Greedily taking the richest house can block two good neighbors.

prompt: Letters are encoded as 1–26. How many ways can a digit string be decoded?
why: ways(i) adds ways(i−1) if the last digit is valid and ways(i−2) if the last two form 10–26.
trap: Enumerating decodings is exponential; counting them is linear.

prompt: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum, where numbers can be negative.
why: Kadane: best ending here = max(x, best ending before + x).
trap: Negatives break a sliding window's shrink rule.

prompt: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
why: lis(i) = 1 + max lis(j) over earlier smaller j. (Patience sorting brings it to O(n log n).)
trap: A subsequence can skip elements, so a window or a stack of neighbors won't capture it.
